description:
Search one store's catalog of extensions fetched so far, for market and niche research:
store "chrome" (default) or "firefox", one per call -- Chrome users are a rounded weekly
count, Firefox's an exact daily average, so the two are never mixed. listed and known in
each answer show how much of that store the catalog covers.
rank is the position by users within the store; ties share a rank (rank_tied = others at the same
count); recomputed weekly on rank_on; rank_change is the move since the week before, positive = up.

Filter by name words (match "all" or "any"; case and punctuation are ignored, and an exact
name comes first unless you sort), by one category of that store (a slug such as
"productivity/developer" or "privacy-security"; an unknown one is refused with the store's
list) and by inclusive ranges on users, rating, reviews, language count and description
length; sort by any of those or by last update. This never fetches the store. users,
rating and reviews are null when the store shows no number, which is not zero. Each row
says whether it is one of yours or a competitor you track; pass its store and id to
add_competitor to start tracking it. For one extension's full listing, call get_listing.

Allows 60 calls a minute per account.

Works without an account too.

category.description: One category slug of the chosen store, as rows return it.

dir.description: Defaults to desc. Nulls always last.

sort.description: Defaults to users, with an exact name match first when query is given.
